blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: On Java 21, many virtual threads each run a slow database query inside the same synchronized block. Per this page, what does that do to their carrier threads?

options.text: Each waiting query keeps its carrier busy, so fewer carriers are left for other virtual threads
options.says: The page says a virtual thread that blocks inside synchronized is pinned: its carrier blocks with it, and with every carrier pinned other virtual threads cannot run.

options.text: Each waiting query gives its carrier back, as it would for a query outside the block
options.says: The page says unmounting is exactly what synchronized prevents on Java 21; only outside such a block, or under a ReentrantLock, does the carrier go free.

options.text: Each waiting query gets a new carrier made for it, so the other virtual threads keep going
options.says: The page says the scheduler does not compensate for pinning inside synchronized; it adds carriers only for some other operations, such as Object.wait().

questions.stem: Per this page, how do you find the code that holds virtual threads on their carriers while testing an application on Java 21?

options.text: Call Thread.getAllStackTraces() and read the entries for the virtual threads
options.says: The page names this as a pitfall: Thread.getAllStackTraces() does not include virtual threads.

options.text: Leave synchronized blocks out, since on Java 21 they no longer pin a thread
options.says: The page says Java 24 (JEP 491) removes pinning for synchronized blocks, but in Java 21 pinning is still a concern.

options.text: Start the JVM with -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full and read the stack traces it prints
options.says: The page's Monitoring Pinning section runs java -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full to print a stack trace when a virtual thread is pinned.

concepts: On Java 21 a virtual thread that blocks inside synchronized pins its carrier, and the scheduler adds no carrier to make up for it.
-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads and the JFR jdk.VirtualThreadPinned event find pinning during development.
